steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: Five years ago, the town of Deeproot was destroyed by a Catastrophe.

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: Thanks to assistance from the Holy City, we were able to rebuild our lives on this new land.

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: Five years later, the new Deeproot is up on its feet. We are now in a position to revive our town's traditional art—sculpture.

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: In the old days, the middle of town always displayed the masterwork of our greatest craftsmen.

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: And now, I would like to revive this tradition and commission a new statue by our best craftsmen, in memory of those who did not survive.

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: Your father was the best craftsman in town, Susan, and we have seen how hard you've worked to carry his mantle. Will you take up this responsibility?

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: I—if Father was still here, there would have been no one more qualified.

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: But for me... I don't know if I'm ready.

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: It's such a heavy burden, to commemorate the departed.

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: I know it's a monumental challenge, but there's no other—

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: If Susan isn't sure, may I try my hand at it?

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: Melissa! You're back from Laterano?

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Your letter said the town was planning to erect a new statue. I set out as soon as I read it.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: I went back to the Holy City with the emissaries, but my heart has always been in Deeproot.

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: Good, very good.

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: You say you want to work on the statue?

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Yes. I honed my skills in Laterano, waiting for the day when I could contribute to the town again.

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: That's very kind of you. In that case...

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: Wait!

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: It was my father who made the statue that stood in the middle of town, before it was destroyed by Catastrophe.

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: It was... special. Everyone in town said they smelled a scent that belonged only to us when they were near it.

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: I believe... the best way to commemorate them is to recreate the same statue.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Can you recreate the scent, though?

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: I-I'm not sure, but I'll try.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Listen, Susan.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: The townsfolk, the ones who are left anyway, won't wait for you to rediscover this 'special' tradition.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Sometimes, it's the continuation that matters.

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: ...I know.

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: (Mutters) The place that Father used to go all the time...

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: (Mutters) It's dangerous, but...

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: Susan! Where are you going?

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: She's headed toward... was I too harsh? I'll bring her back—

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I'll take care of Susan.

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: Is that—Mostima?!

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Mostima?!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Mayor, Melissa. How long as it been?

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: It's good to see you. How are the rest of your team, Andoain and the others?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Heh... they're good.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Let's talk later.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: You're Melissa, right? You must be!

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: You're—

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: I brought you the materials you needed for the sculpture!

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: By the way, have you seen a Sankta by the name of Mostima?

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: (Mutters) Did you pick this time to come back on purpose, Mostima?

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Where did Mostima go?

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: She went into the hills.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Won't be back for a while.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Ah—alright.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: I'll help out here, then!

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: You'll just do whatever she dumps on you?

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: I've been looking for her for a while.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Every time I go to a new place, I happen across something like this, something that's just as much fun as looking for her.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Sounds like she's doing it on purpose.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Who knows? But that's just Mostima.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: When we were little, she never came along when I asked her to blow stuff up with me.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: But there were a few times when I realized that she was watching me from a distance.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: How do you know Mostima?

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Our town, Deeproot, was destroyed by a Catastrophe five years ago.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: My father and I were the only surviving Sanktas.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: The Holy City received my father's call for help and sent a squad to pick us up.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: (My sister's old squad...)

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: But their leader, Andoain, didn't just take us away.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Together with his cohorts, he escorted the non-Sankta refugees to this place.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: They also requested supplies from the Holy City. It's only later that I learned they had taken out a year's wages in advance to do this.

a.text: You asked me why my brow is furrowed, Mostima.
I ask you instead: Can you look at yourself in the mirror, and see no shame or regret?
This is all we can do for these non-Sankta refugees.
All we can do is to take them to a patch of new soil, send them some supplies, and take our own people back to Laterano.
What happens here is none of our concern. There's a life of beauty and happiness waiting for us back home.
This has been taken for granted.
We've accepted it, and so have they.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: El should have started working at Melissa's place now.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Melissa knows enough of my past to satisfy her a bit.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Found you, Susan.

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: My father used to come here.

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: You could see the whole town from this place.

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: Whenever he was in a bad mood, he would come here and look out at the town in the distance.

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: He used to say that memory isn't just the storage of information. He wanted those who touched the statue to recall the scent of the old days.

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: But, Father... all I see when I stand here now is a broken ruin.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: That statue, it's damaged, but still standing.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I'll be right back.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Wow, this is a huge rock.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: It's not just for one statue, is it?

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Correct. My plan is to sculpt a set of statues to commemorate the dead.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: You've seen similar sets of statues in Laterano, haven't you?

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Oh, like the ones on the plaza?

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Yes. I wanted to sculpt a set of statues like those, and inscribe the names of the dead.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Sounds like the murals in the churches.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: You're a smart girl.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: You said you started sculpting only after you went back to Laterano?

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Yes. Deeproot was known for its sculptures, but not everyone was a sculptor.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: I was one of the non-sculptors.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Honestly, I had difficulty adjusting to life in Laterano.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Maybe I'd just been used to Deeproot, so the constant joyful jubilation in Laterano hardly feels right to me.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Ah—I get that.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: I've been following Mostima's trail for a couple of years, and seen a lot of places outside of Laterano. I've come to realize that they're very different from the Holy City.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: You know, one of my dreams is to live in a different city.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Then you're not just a happy-go-lucky girl, are you?

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Anyway, it wasn't until I went to Laterano that I became interested in sculpting, and began to pursue it formally.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: In my heart, I always wanted to come back here.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: But Lateran sculptures aren't the same as the ones here, are they?

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: ...I know that.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: When I began to seriously study sculpture, I also began to regret not studying Deeproot sculpting while the town was still around.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: The past can't be changed, though. I'll continue the tradition here with Lateran techniques.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Unless somebody knows a better way.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: So you're hoping Susan succeeds?

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: ...You must be joking. I won't let five years of hard work go to waste.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: The largest rock over here.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Gotcha.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Anyway, if you want to help, you can start by cutting the rocks down to the required size.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: In Lateran terms—

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Blow 'em up!

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: *sigh* I knew it. Just don't go too far and turn it into a heap of rubble.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Don't worry, I'm an explosives expert!
Time has taken its toll on the streets, which are filled with mud and scattered bricks and rubble. The marks left by Catastrophe are everywhere.
Even the most experienced Messengers avoid such places, but Mostima steps inside without hesitation, stopping only to tighten her hood.
She has gotten far too used to such environments in the span of just two years.
Five years ago, she would not have gone to such lengths. Indeed, she might not have stood here at all.
In the two years that she has been a Legatus, however, she has seen too many places and things that she had never seen before.
When she set foot in the place, she already had an inkling of what Susan was talking about.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: The answer to the scent might be a simple one.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: You think so too, don't you?
Mostima comes before the statue that stands in the middle of the ruins, carefully removes a broken piece, and takes a sniff of it.
Then, she bends down and picks up a handful of soil, and takes a sniff from it as well.
It is as she thought.
The secret to this 'scent of the town' is simple—
It is a mingled scent of the soil and the stone used in sculpting.
And there is no great secret to why the townsfolk found it familiar. It has the freshness that the vegetation left in the soil, and the unique mineral scent of the stone.
The townsfolk have lived side-by-side with these scents all their lives, which combined to become a scent that brought back memories to the people who lived here.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Can't say it's that pleasant.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Then again, we've been all over, but we've never smelled a smell quite like it, have we?

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Explosives, set.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: I've done the math. You'll get the result you want when it goes off!

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: You really know what you're doing, don't you? Couldn't tell at first glance.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: I told you, I'm an explosives expert!

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Let's get started! Boom!
Lemuel's math was on-point.
The massive rock cracks into several pieces as the explosions go off.
The only thing she neglected was the nature of the stone.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: By the way, did I tell you that these rocks emit a large amount of dust when detonated?
Lemuel cannot open her eyes in the thick dust that fills the entire area.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: I-I can't see!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: What the...?

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Mosti—

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Shh—

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: I can't see! Melissa, help!

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Look out! There's a hole in the ground—

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Huh? Whoa—!
Lemuel's foot finds nothing but empty air. Her body instantly thrown off balance.
As she is about to fall into the hole, a hand grabs her arm and pulls her back.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Thanks, Melissa—

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Gotta be more careful, El.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Mostima?!
Hearing the familiar voice, Lemuel rubs her eyes and forces them open.
But she sees no one before her.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: *cough* *cough* Mostima?!

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Melissa? Was Mostima just here a moment ago?

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Melissa? Where did you go?

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: What's going on?!!

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: This scent...

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: Yes, that's it... mm... oh...

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: It's exactly what Deeproot used to smell like...

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: This is the scent alright.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: I didn't think it would be so simple.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: It's the simplest things that leave the deepest impression.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: I... have to thank you for finding it, Mostima, Susan.

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: It's me who should be thanking you, Melissa.

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: Without you, I would still be going around in circles.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Well, it's a little too early to celebrate.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: If the secret behind the scent is so simple, there's no reason why I can't use it.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Now ain't that a cunning move.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: You didn't think the townsfolk would pick you just because you discovered the scent?

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: No, I'll sculpt the best statue!

steps.name: Humble Mayor
steps.text: I don't know how to thank you, Mostima. You helped the town discover that familiar scent, and brought vitality back to the place.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: You flatter me, Mr. Mayor... I just happened to be in the right place at the right time.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: But I'm curious, Mostima.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Five years ago, all you did was follow your squad leader Andoain, without saying a single word.

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Why did you come today to do all this for us?
When she arrived on scene, what she saw was a gravely injured Lemuen, and a crazed Andoain who had committed the act.
She sensed many emotions in that instant—bewilderment, hysteria, alongside relief and acceptance.
It put a doubt in her heart, but did not stop her from acting.
To stop Andoain, she had to knock the Lock and Key from his hand with her patron firearm. She left with Lemuen after retrieving the Lock and Key.
They returned to Laterano, accompanied by Fiammetta.
After that, the Lock and Key were taken from her, and she was put under house arrest.
She did not regret her fall. It was what Andoain saw in the Lock and Key that she was more concerned about.
She made the bold decision to break into the Curia.
Miss this chance, and the secret may elude her forever.
Infiltrating the Curia was not easy, but she succeeded.
Thinking back now, the white-bearded old man must have had a hand in it. He would hardly have allowed Mostima to keep the Lock and Key otherwise.
Whatever the reason, she was once again in possession of the Lock and Key.
The Lock and Key did not react when she took them from Andoain.
This time, when she touched them again with questions in her heart, she walked into a fantastical plane.
There, she saw—
A gap in the past. A cross-section of the future.
She has a pretty good guess as to what Andoain saw.
When she saw what she saw on that plane, she immediately understood why Andoain went mad.
After all, Andoain was always worried about the future, always lamenting over the smallest of tragedies.
In a way, she could even say that Fiammetta's anger at Andoain's actions was born out of Fiammetta's approval of him—

Considering Fiammetta's sense of justice, it is no wonder that she always held Andoain in high regard for the concern he showed for others, in comparison to Fiammetta herself, who always seemed a little aloof and removed.
However, Mostima was not obsessed with the reasons for Andoain's madness. It was not simply because of the emotions that she sensed from the pair at that instant.
Instead, it is because she had a feeling, a feeling that she had perhaps harbored from the moment she joined Andoain's squad, even the moment she first saw Andoain—
They were walking divergent paths, and it was inevitable that they must go their separate ways.

It was like the many thousands of pieces before her eyes, each one potentially revealing the answer to a question. Perhaps the answer to the ultimate question will reveal itself when all the pieces are exhausted.
Andoain will choose to walk toward those pieces without hesitation, stepping into the dark mire where the stars shine.
As for her—she chose to turn back.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: When I saw what I saw, I thought—

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Oh, how terrible.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I didn't feel anything else.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: That's why I didn't understand the struggle that a certain somebody was going through.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: But now—

steps.name: Hesitant Woman
steps.text: Mostima, those horns...

steps.name: Staid Woman
steps.text: Are you fallen?!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: These past two years, I've traveled the lands as a Legatus, and I've come to a conclusion—

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Lovely bastards, the Sanktas are.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I've just relearned how to live with this land, after realizing that I was a bastard.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Tell El that I have a new mission. I'll be in Lungmen for a while.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I ran into this guy by the name of 'Emperor' six months ago. He's in Lungmen too. I think I'll pay him a visit.
Mostima turns around at the hillside.
She can see the town square in the distance.
Susan and Melissa have already started their preparations. A crowd has assembled to watch them, and it is growing bigger.
The red hair of a certain Sankta stands out in the crowd. She goes from one side to another, helping out here and there, seemingly having forgotten why she was here in the first place.
For once, Mostima is not wearing her hood. She lets the breeze brush against her cheeks and run through her hair.

a.text: I think I understand you a little better now, Andoain.
Maybe I should have had a few more drinks with you. Maybe I should have let you have more time together with Lemuen.
Alright, I know, you were always going to leave in the end.
But there's something that I want to say.
Now that I've gotten to know you better, I can say with certainty—
I won't make the same choices you did.
Nothing can bear the burden of the happiness of all the people. Not you, not me, not even Laterano.
All we can do is to focus on what we can see.
Just like I've been taking El around these past two years, fulfilling a little of the responsibility I bear for her coming out of Laterano to find me. That's all.
I don't hate you like Fiammetta does. But don't expect a warm welcome when we meet again.
Wherever that might be, our journey will take us there.
